params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# The tool DECLARATIONS of this hive, in the hive, beside the cells they
# describe.
#
# WHY THEY LIVE HERE AND NOT IN THE OCCUPANTS. A tool cell declares its
# MESSAGE contract -- which body slots it consumes, which hop keys it emits --
# and that is a different document from the one a model reads: `contract`
# answers "what does the substrate carry", a schema answers "what may I fill
# in". No occupant of this hive publishes the second one anywhere a machine can
# read; today the argument shape is prose in `description.consumes_meaning` and
# an example line. So this table is the FIRST machine-readable copy, not a
# second one, and the drift lock that holds it to the dispatch graph is what
# keeps it the only one.
#
# ADDING A TOOL IS STILL ONE CHANGE INSIDE THIS HIVE: one occupant directory,
# two edges, one row here.
SCHEMAS = {
    "bash": {
        "description":
            "Run one shell command and get its output back. One-shot: no "
            "session, no shell state and no working directory carried from one "
            "call to the next -- a call that needs one writes `cd /x && cmd`. A "
            "non-zero exit code is an ordinary result, not a failure of the "
            "call.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "command": {"type": "string",
                            "description": "the command line to run"}},
            "required": ["command"]}},
    "web_fetch": {
        "description":
            "Fetch one URL with GET and get the response body back. GET only: "
            "no method, header or body control, and no retries. A non-2xx "
            "status is an ordinary result.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "url": {"type": "string",
                        "description": "the absolute URL to fetch"}},
            "required": ["url"]}},
    "web_search": {
        "description":
            "Query the configured search endpoint and get the result list back "
            "-- title, url and snippet per hit. No ranking and no pagination of "
            "its own; an empty list is an ordinary result.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "query": {"type": "string",
                          "description": "what to search for"}},
            "required": ["query"]}},
    "file": {
        "description":
            "Read, write, list or stat a file under this assistant's file "
            "root. Every path is relative to that root and anything reaching "
            "outside it is refused.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "op": {"type": "string",
                       "enum": ["read", "write", "list", "stat"]},
                "path": {"type": "string",
                         "description": "path relative to the file root"},
                "content": {"type": "string",
                            "description": "the text to write (op=write)"},
                "mode": {"type": "string", "enum": ["text", "base64"],
                         "description": "how to return the payload (op=read)"},
                "offset": {"type": "integer",
                           "description": "first byte to read (op=read)"},
                "limit": {"type": "integer",
                          "description": "how many bytes to read (op=read)"}},
            "required": ["op", "path"]}},
    "edit": {
        "description":
            "Change a file in place under this assistant's file root. "
            "`find_replace` replaces EVERY occurrence and refuses when the "
            "pattern is not there; pass `expected_matches` to make the count a "
            "precondition instead of a report. `insert_at_line` is 1-based and "
            "inserts BEFORE the line named.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "op": {"type": "string",
                       "enum": ["find_replace", "insert_at_line"]},
                "path": {"type": "string",
                         "description": "path relative to the file root"},
                "find": {"type": "string",
                         "description": "the literal text to replace "
                                        "(op=find_replace)"},
                "replace": {"type": "string",
                            "description": "what to put there "
                                           "(op=find_replace)"},
                "expected_matches": {
                    "type": "integer",
                    "description": "refuse unless exactly this many "
                                   "occurrences were found (op=find_replace)"},
                "line": {"type": "integer",
                         "description": "1-based line to insert before "
                                        "(op=insert_at_line)"},
                "content": {"type": "string",
                            "description": "the text to insert "
                                           "(op=insert_at_line)"}},
            "required": ["op", "path"]}},
    "build_topology": {
        "description":
            "Ask the colony's builder to DRAFT a manifest -- an ordered list of "
            "mutation declarations. Nothing is applied by this call; the answer "
            "carries the manifest and the sha256 digest that `apply_manifest` "
            "needs.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "request": {"type": "string",
                            "description": "what should exist, in plain "
                                           "language"},
                "scope": {"type": "string",
                          "description": "the path every declaration must name "
                                         "or stand under"},
                "recipe": {"type": "string",
                           "enum": ["rewire_edge", "add_node",
                                    "attach_drain", "grow_level"],
                           "description":
                               "a predefined recipe, when the request is "
                               "exactly one of these -- the builder renders it "
                               "without asking a model. `rewire_edge` moves one "
                               "existing edge to a new target. `add_node` grows "
                               "one cell from a template under the scope and "
                               "wires it to a target on a route. `attach_drain` "
                               "draws one further out-edge from a node that is "
                               "already there. `grow_level` grows one whole "
                               "LEVEL of the composition -- an org, member, "
                               "assistant, channel, screen or app -- from a "
                               "template into the container that level lives "
                               "in, together with the transit edges the parent "
                               "always gives a child of that level, as ONE "
                               "declaration -- optionally asleep, and "
                               "optionally with the identity door drawn beside "
                               "it (see `params`). Leave the slot out and the "
                               "request is DESIGNED instead of rendered.",
                           },
                "params": {"type": "object",
                           "description":
                               "the named recipe's parameters. `grow_level` "
                               "always needs `scope`, `level`, `name` and "
                               "`template`, plus `assistant` for a channel and "
                               "`screen` for an app. Four are optional: `ctx` "
                               "and `override_params` as in any declaration; "
                               "`birth` (`active` or `inactive`) to place the "
                               "whole subtree registered but TASKLESS, which a "
                               "channel does by default; and, on an assistant, "
                               "`subscribe`, which draws the push edge from the "
                               "member's own affinity record into it so the "
                               "agent can be told who it is talking to, and "
                               "`credential`, which grows the generation with "
                               "NO provider key of its own -- its brains ask "
                               "the member's own broker for one over a v-lane. "
                               "`credential` takes `cred_ref`, `subject` and "
                               "`expires_at`, and renders a second declaration "
                               "beside the level."}},
            "required": ["request"]}},
    "apply_manifest": {
        "description":
            "Submit a manifest that `build_topology` drafted, under your own "
            "identity. Send the manifest list and the digest exactly as they "
            "came back: re-rendering or re-ordering them changes the bytes, and "
            "the submitter refuses its own colony's draft.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "manifest": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"},
                             "description": "the declaration list from the "
                                            "draft, verbatim"},
                "manifest_sha256": {"type": "string",
                                    "description": "the digest the draft came "
                                                   "with"}},
            "required": ["manifest", "manifest_sha256"]}},
}

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc["body"]
asked = body.get("tools")

# ABSENT and EMPTY are two different requests and must not look alike. A caller
# that declared no tools gets no schemas -- that is an answer. A request that
# carries no `tools` slot at all lost it on the way, and saying so is cheaper
# than a menu the caller never asked for.
if not isinstance(asked, list):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "schemas", "error_code": "tools_missing",
                   "schema_count": 0, "unknown_count": 0},
        "schemas": [], "unknown": [],
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "the request carried no `tools` list"}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)]
if "*" in names:
    wanted, unknown = sorted(SCHEMAS), []
else:
    seen, wanted, unknown = set(), [], []
    for n in names:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        (wanted if n in SCHEMAS else unknown).append(n)

schemas = [dict(name=n, **SCHEMAS[n]) for n in wanted]
header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    # Named, never dropped. The caller reads the refusal off the message the
    # same way it reads a tool's own -- one lane, `hop.error_code` tells them
    # apart -- and a partial answer is still an answer: the schemas it DID find
    # travel beside it.
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown, "messages": []}))

description.purpose: The DECLARATIONS of this hive's tools, handed out by name: a request naming tool names comes back as their JSON schemas, and a name nobody wired comes back in `unknown` rather than as a silence.
description.use_when: Reached on the hive's `in_schemas` lane, once, when a cell that uses tools starts up and asks for exactly the names its own template declares. Never addressed by name and never part of a tool round -- it answers no `tool_call` and carries no `tool_name`.
description.not_in_scope: No judgement about which tools a caller SHOULD have -- whoever wrote that template decided, and this cell hands out what was asked for. No table of who asked: a subscriber list here would be a second copy of a decision that is already visible in the caller's own contract. And no provider envelope: the answer is {name, description, parameters} per tool, and wrapping that in whatever shape a model provider wants is the caller's business, because the caller is the one that knows its provider.
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: one {name, description, parameters} per tool that exists, in the order asked (sorted, for `*`). unknown[]: the names that matched nothing, verbatim. hop.error_code `tool_unknown` when that list is non-empty, `tools_missing` when the request carried no `tools` slot at all -- an absent list and an empty one are two different requests.
description.consumes_meaning: body.tools: the names this caller declares it uses, e.g. ["web_search","web_fetch"]. The single entry ["*"] asks for every tool the hive has.
examples: {"tools":["*"]} -> every schema the hive carries, sorted by name
